reader.summary: Germany's week was defined by a major political scandal and layered security concerns. Hacked emails from the far-right AfD party were released, exposing internal communications and rocking party leadership, while the AfD launched an investigation into the breach. Simultaneously, a Ukrainian man was arrested in northeastern Germany on suspicion of spying for Russia, prompting Chancellor Merz to warn that Germany faces "intensive" Russian espionage and that Europe is underestimating the threat. A fire devastated Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat in the Bavarian Alps, with a suspect detained. On the economic front, investor confidence fell for the first time in six months, the Bundesbank indicated the economy likely stagnated in the third quarter, and industry has lost nearly half a million jobs since 2019. The 2026 Invest in Germany Summit attracted pledges including Amazon's $17 billion expansion, but the event was shadowed by controversy over Berlin's plan to seize landlords' apartments, which top landlords called a signal that Germany is "uninvestable." Gas use hit a nine-month high as cold weather boosted demand, and a novice driver caused a security incident at Leipzig airport. Germany also summoned Iran's envoy over a plot to kill German Jewish community leaders, and youth groups announced plans for France-style mass protests.

key_events.event: Hacked emails from the AfD party were publicly released, revealing internal communications and prompting the party to investigate the cyberattack.
A Ukrainian man was arrested in northeastern Germany on suspicion of spying for Russia, and Chancellor Merz warned of "intensive" Russian espionage targeting Germany.
Investor confidence and ZEW morale declined for the first time in six months as the Bundesbank indicated the economy likely stagnated in the third quarter.
The 2026 Invest in Germany Summit drew major pledges including Amazon's $17 billion expansion, but Berlin's apartment-seizure plan raised fears among landlords that Germany is "uninvestable."
A fire devastated Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat in the Bavarian Alps, and a suspect was detained.
Germany summoned Iran's envoy after Tehran was linked to a plot to kill leaders of German Jewish community groups.
Two men turned themselves in after smashing their car into a fence at Leipzig airport, triggering a security investigation.
German gas use hit a nine-month high as cold weather boosted power demand, and the government secured extra winter gas supplies as storage levels lagged.
German youth groups announced plans for France-style mass protests, adding to social pressure on the government.

display.eli5:
Germany is going through a rough week. A bunch of hackers stole private emails from the far-right AfD party and published them, and now the party is fighting internally about what the emails reveal about their leader. Think of it like a group chat getting leaked and everyone arguing about who said what.

At the same time, a man from Ukraine was arrested in Germany because police think he was spying for Russia. The chancellor said there are probably more spies out there and that Europe is underestimating the threat. So expect more arrests or a big government briefing about it.

The government is also trying to attract big investments like Amazon spending seventeen billion dollars, while at the same time planning to take apartments from landlords in Berlin. The landlords are furious and calling Germany uninvestable. The coalition will probably have to make a formal decision on this soon.

A surprise could be the youth groups actually holding their big protests in multiple cities, which would add another layer of pressure on the government.
